takeaway: Six JPA entities in two unconnected clusters: Owner owns Pets which own Visits (cascade ALL), each Pet has exactly one PetType; Vets and Specialties are many-to-many through vet_specialties.

elements.name: Owner
elements.responsibility: table owners; lastName indexed and searched by prefix; telephone validated as 10 digits

elements.name: Pet
elements.responsibility: table pets; name unique per owner (unique_owner_pet_name)

elements.name: Visit
elements.responsibility: table visits; date column visit_date, description max 255

elements.name: PetType
elements.responsibility: table types; lookup of pet kinds

relations.label: pets: 0..1 to 0..*, composition (cascade ALL, FK pets.owner_id nullable)
visits: 0..1 to 0..*, composition (cascade ALL, FK visits.pet_id nullable)

concern_details.detail: relationships with multiplicities from the JPA mappings

omitted.name: BaseEntity, NamedEntity, Person
omitted.reason: @MappedSuperclass, no tables of their own; their id/name/firstName/lastName columns are folded into the subclasses (note + shown attributes)

omitted.name: firstName, address, Pet/Vet getters and helper methods
omitted.reason: not key for the data model; public operations are not needed for this concern

omitted.name: MySQL and PostgreSQL schema variants
omitted.reason: same tables; H2 schema used as the reference, differences (e.g. VARCHAR_IGNORECASE) not shown

omitted.name: Repositories and queries
omitted.reason: access paths, not data; the only one that touches indexing (findByLastNameStartingWith) is reflected as {indexed} on Owner.lastName
